```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

`medrev` takes a research question to a folder of open-access PDFs plus the
audit tables a literature review needs. The retrieval and curation steps are
deterministic; an optional enrichment layer adds model-assisted summary and
synthesis on top, with the model call supplied by you.

Every code chunk below reaches the network, so this vignette is not evaluated;
run the pieces yourself.

```{r}
library(medrev)
```

## 1. Configure

Unpaywall (one of the PDF resolvers) needs a contact e-mail. Europe PMC does
not, but it is polite to set one.

```{r}
options(medrev.email = "you@example.org")   # or set the MEDREV_EMAIL env var
```

## 2. Search

`pubmed()` searches Europe PubMed Central, which indexes all of PubMed and
MEDLINE. Supply a topic or a Europe PMC field expression.

```{r}
r <- pubmed("interpretable machine learning for sepsis prognosis",
            n = 400, years = c(2015, 2025))
r
```

Add a second query, or a set of identifiers, with `add()`; scan medRxiv /
bioRxiv for very recent preprints with `preprints()` and merge with `c()`.

```{r}
r <- add(r, "sepsis mortality prediction deep learning", n = 200)
pp <- preprints("sepsis machine learning prognosis", "medrxiv", from = "2025-01-01")
r <- c(r, pp)
search_log(r)
```

## 3. De-duplicate

Exact identifier matches first, then near-identical titles when
`fuzzy = TRUE`. Borderline title matches are kept and listed for a manual
look rather than dropped.

```{r}
r <- dedup(r, fuzzy = TRUE)
attr(r, "duplicate_audit")
attr(r, "review_candidates")
```

## 4. Screen

Screen by condition (evaluated against the record table, as in `subset()`):

```{r}
r <- screen(r, exclude = year < 2016, reason = "pre-2016 protocol")
r <- screen(r,
            exclude = !grepl("machine learning|deep learning|neural network",
                             tolower(paste(title, abstract))),
            reason = "not an ML study")
```

or hand-screen in a spreadsheet:

```{r}
screen(r, file = "screen.csv")     # fill the `decision` column, then:
r <- screen(r, sheet = "screen.csv")
```

## 5. Describe the corpus

```{r}
year_counts(r, which = "included")
term_counts(r, "mesh", top = 20)
```

## 6. Resolve and download open-access PDFs

`resolve()` attaches a PDF link from Europe PMC full text, then Unpaywall,
then the publisher `citation_pdf_url` tag. Links are cached on disk, so
re-running a review that overlaps a previous one is nearly free.

```{r}
r <- resolve(r)
table(as.data.frame(r)$pdf_source, useNA = "ifany")

dl <- fetch(r, dir = "sepsis_pdfs", which = "included", name = "{year}_{pmid}")
dl
```

`fetch()` rejects responses that are not actually PDFs (paywall or error
pages) and logs them as failures. `limit =` caps the number of downloads.

## 7. Study flow and references

```{r}
prisma(r)
bibliography(r, "sepsis.ris", which = "included")   # .ris / .bib / .csv by extension
```

## 8. Model-assisted synthesis (optional)

The enrichment verbs take a **model callback**: any function that accepts a
prompt string and returns the model's text response. `medrev` builds the
grounded prompts and parses the responses; generated content is kept in a
`medrev_insights` table and never written back into the records.

Here is a callback that calls the Claude API over HTTP:

```{r}
claude <- function(prompt, ...) {
  resp <- httr2::request("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages") |>
    httr2::req_headers(
      "x-api-key" = Sys.getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"),
      "anthropic-version" = "2023-06-01"
    ) |>
    httr2::req_body_json(list(
      model = "claude-opus-5",
      max_tokens = 1024,
      messages = list(list(role = "user", content = prompt))
    )) |>
    httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 3) |>
    httr2::req_perform()
  httr2::resp_body_json(resp)$content[[1]]$text
}
```

`llm_echo()` is a deterministic stub if you just want to see the plumbing
move.

```{r}
ch  <- chunk(r, which = "included")            # abstracts; pass fulltext(r) for full text
sm  <- summarize(ch, llm = claude)             # one grounded summary per study
ex  <- extract(ch, llm = claude,
               fields = c(design  = "study design",
                          n       = "total sample size",
                          outcome = "primary outcome",
                          auc     = "reported discrimination (AUC/C-index)"))
extractions(ex)                                # one row per study, a column per field
syn <- synthesize(c(sm, ex), llm = claude)     # cross-study synthesis

review_brief(r, insights = c(sm, ex, syn),
             title = "Interpretable ML for sepsis prognosis: rapid brief",
             file  = "brief.md")
```

The brief is Markdown: the search log, the PRISMA flow, the synthesis, a
per-study block (citation plus its summary and extracted fields), and a
numbered reference list of the included studies.

## The `medrev` object

One carrier holds the whole review:

- `as.data.frame(r)` -- the record table (a `basetable`) with a stable schema.
- `r$searches` -- one row per `pubmed()` / `add()` / `preprints()` call.
- `r$stages` -- the row count after each pipeline step, which is what
  `prisma()` reads.

`r[i, ]` subsets the records; `c()` merges reviews.
